extractions.value: Clinical features (stiffness and spasms in left leg, stimulus sensitivity, no truncal rigidity or lumbar hyperlordosis), EMG (continuous low-frequency firing of normal motor unit potentials in tibialis anterior muscle), anti-GAD antibodies highly increased (>2000 U/ml), normal CSF, response to diazepam and IVIG.
extractions.quote: Because stiff leg syndrome was suspect ed, antiglutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) antibodies were assayed and found to be highly increased (>2000 U/ml; normal <5 U/ml). ... EMG showed a typical pattern of continuous low-frequency firing of normal motor unit potentials indistinguishable from voluntary muscle contraction in the tibialis anterior muscle ... Diazepam 5 mg twice daily and monthly intravenous immunoglobulin infusions led to significant clinical improvement. A diagnosis of stiff leg syndrome was made.

extractions.value: Isolated hypertrophy of the tibialis anterior muscle was noted, which the authors state has never been described in stiff person or stiff leg syndrome. MRI of the lower limbs confirmed isolated hypertrophy of the tibialis anterior muscle.
extractions.quote: To the best of our knowledge, muscle hypertrophy has never been described in the stiff person or stiff leg syndrome. ... Isolated tibialis anterior muscle hypertrophy in our patient seemed to be related to persistent muscle contraction, as has been seen in other muscle disorders associated with involuntary muscle contraction (e.g., myotonic syndromes, rippling muscle syndrome, and dystonia).
